source.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories
source.authors: Jun Guo; Piao-Piao Jin; Jason Li; Pei-Yan Li; Ying-Yan Li; Fu-Teng Liu; Wan-Li Peng; Optimus Qin; Yifei Su; Nan Sun; Qiao Sun; Run-Ze Suo; He-Yun Wang; Yun-Hong Wang; Ru-Jie Wu; Cao-Yu Xia; Li-Na Zhang; Jack Zhao; Guo-Liang Chen; Wen-Long Chen; Xin He; Bin Li; Qing Li; Zhuo Li; Heng-Xu Qu; Wen-Xuan Song; Di-Yun Xiang; Yi-Fan Xie; Pei-Ran Xu; Hang-Jun Ye; Wen Ye; Han Zhao; Quan-Yun Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, but several figures are garbled in the extraction, so their plotted values cannot be read.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies scaling in a new setting: vision-language-action robot policies, using validation action error and downstream robot success rather than language-model cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports robot action-error and success-rate results as scale changes. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit power laws, test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or report predictive fits. Cited language-model scaling results are not the paper's own results.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (robot VLA policies built on a VLM), the paper reports its own downstream real-robot success rates across pretraining data fractions (5B) and model sizes (2B/5B/10B). This bears on V6. It fits no power law, extrapolation, compute-optimal split or shape result, and does not measure language-model cross-entropy.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that performance improves consistently with pretraining data scale and model size, and that this transfers to better out-of-the-box post-training success. They add that data, rather than model capacity, is the main bottleneck at billion-parameter scale. They fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a robot VLA scaling study using held-out action MSE and real-robot task success, not language-model cross-entropy, token/compute sweeps, or power-law fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: At 12.5% and 25% of the data-scaling corpus, validation action error first falls and then rises; the 50% and 100% settings decrease monotonically. The 5B and 10B models give comparable sofa-tidying rates (80% and 77%).

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out validation action MSE of the robot VLA falls with more UMI pretraining data; the 12.5% and 25% runs overfit and were stopped early. MSE also falls with model size 2B to 10B, with smaller gaps than across data scales. No power law is fitted and values are figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In robot VLA pretraining, held-out action error improves with data and model size, with data the main bottleneck at billion-parameter scale, but small-data runs overfit.

record.code_released: Code and model checkpoints will be released; URL not stated.
record.problems: The scaling figures are not numerically readable in the supplied extraction. The paper does not fit power laws or report uncertainty for the scaling results, and the real-robot scaling evaluation is reported on four tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No additional readable numerical scaling outcomes were available from the garbled plots. Simulation benchmark comparisons and fine-tuning comparisons do not measure performance as a function of pretraining scale for the claim versions tested here.

untested.parts: No language-model cross-entropy and no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from fitted small runs.
Robot action-error trends with data and model size are reported, but the power-law form is never fitted, so the 'same form' claim is untested.
'Predictably' is untested: no fitted relation of success to scale or to pretraining loss, and only three to five points per sweep on four tasks without uncertainty.

missing.what: Per-task success rates for bag packing and table organization in both sweeps, and the 25% and 50% data per-task values. Text says model scaling improves three of four tasks.
Authors note marginal gains moderate as pretraining data grows but show no saturation (+6 pts from 50% to 100%), a diminishing-returns shape relevant to predictability.

record.verdict_notes: The system is a VLM-based robot policy, not a language model, so V6 applies only by extension to a new setting (T3). Language-model scaling law references [22, 27] are cited only. The simulation benchmark and fine-tuning comparisons are method-versus-baselines results and are rightly left out. The text reports 57.4% versus 57.6% inconsistently for RoboCasa365, which is irrelevant to this claim.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy and power-law fits in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation from small language-model runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between parameter count and token count, including its trend with compute.
Effects of architecture shape, such as depth and width, at fixed parameter count.
The power-law form itself is not fitted or tested. The paper reports robot action-error scaling trends, recorded under fits_no_version.

The paper tests post-training out-of-the-box success across pretraining data scales and model sizes, but not a fitted relationship to pretraining loss or broad downstream benchmarks as a function of scale.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices, and bending of fitted power-law curves.

relationships.condition: Overall out-of-the-box robot success across the pretraining-data sweep (5B) and the model-size sweep (20k h)
relationships.reason: Overall success rises monotonically: 26% with no action pretraining, 53% at 12.5%, about 69% at 50%, 75% at 100%; and 61%/75%/79% at 2B/5B/10B (R8-R15). This is monotonic improvement only, with no predictive fit.
relationships.display_finding: Overall success rises from 26% without action pretraining to 53%, about 69%, and 75% at 12.5%, 50%, and 100% data, respectively, and from 61% to 75% to 79% at 2B, 5B, and 10B parameters, without a predictive fit.

relationships.condition: Shoe-tidying task, model-size sweep and full-data versus no-pretraining
relationships.reason: Success climbs from 58% to 75% to 92% with model size, and from 0% (baseline) to 75% with full pretraining data (R16-R18, R21).
relationships.display_finding: On shoe tidying, success rises from 58% to 75% to 92% with model size and from 0% without pretraining to 75% with full pretraining data.

relationships.reason: The 10B model (77%) does not beat 5B (80%), so per-task gains from model scaling are not uniform (R19-R20).
relationships.display_finding: The 10B model achieved 77% success compared with 80% for 5B.
